purpose: Public measured datasets that constrain the Q017 cardiorenal-transient model in inputs/Q017_model.py
frozen_requirements: PREREG.md 'Frysade dataset-krav': every post carries (a) landing URL answering HTTP 200 at check time, (b) license string copied verbatim from the source's own page, (c) size in bytes/MB from the source's file index, (d) file format, (e) number of subjects with a source, (f) which model parameter or output it constrains, (g) verification status in {downloaded_parsed, listing_verified_only, metadata_only}. Posts without a substantive (a) and (b) are not counted as candidates.
http_check_method: curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -L --max-time 25 -A 'Mozilla/5.0' <url>, run 2026-09-26 from this session; page text read with scripts/fetch_page.py and with an inline tag-stripper, saved under web_evidence/

whole_release.source: PhysioNet file index table on the landing page, sizes summed

posts.integrity: all 6 downloaded data files match the sha256 values in the publisher's own samples/eicu_crd_demo_2.0.1/SHA256SUMS.txt; local digests in samples/SHA256SUMS_LOCAL.txt
caveats: the demo is a de-identified convenience subset, not a random sample of ICU admissions

posts.name: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey, 2017-2018 cycle (US CDC/NCHS)
posts.license_verbatim_available_text: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey / 2017-2018 Data Documentation, Codebook, and Frequencies / Standard Biochemistry Profile (BIOPRO_J) / Data File: BIOPRO_J.xpt / First Published: February 2020 / Last Revised: NA
posts.operational_terms_verified: all 5 .xpt files were downloaded from the CDC URLs with no login, no data use agreement, no application form and no payment; the CDC file index at https://wwwn.cdc.gov/nchs/nhanes/search/datapage.aspx?Component=2017-2018 (HTTP 200) offers the same files to anyone
posts.license_caveat: this is the one frozen field (b) that could not be filled with a verbatim licence string: the modern CDC pages carry no licence block, and the CDC terms-of-use pages either soft-404 with HTTP 200 or answer HTTP 403 to this client. No licence claim is asserted beyond the verified no-DUA public download. Treated as a US federal work in the public domain is an assumption, not a verified quotation.
posts.d_format: SAS XPORT transport (.xpt), one row per examined participant, wide format; codebook pages give per-variable counts and ranges

e_subjects.source: row counts measured in this run from the four .xpt files; the CDC codebook pages independently report 6401 records for BIOPRO_J (5901 non-missing uric acid + 500 missing), which matches the parsed file

posts.integrity: sha256 of all 5 files recorded in samples/SHA256SUMS_LOCAL.txt; no publisher-side checksum file is published for the NHANES .xpt downloads, so the sha256 is a local record, not a publisher match
caveats: no survey weights (SDMVPSU/SDMVSTRA) are applied: all NHANES numbers are unweighted cycle medians/means, not population estimates
cross-sectional by design: no within-participant time axis, so NHANES cannot supply a transient, only a distribution
DXX_J gives fat/lean/bone compartments but no total body water, so the ECF fraction of body mass behind V0 stays unconstrained by this dataset

posts.d_format: gzip-compressed CSV, one file per table (PostgreSQL/other load scripts also published)

e_subjects.source: landing page abstract, verbatim: 'MIMIC-IV contains data for over 65,000 patients admitted to an ICU'

f_constrains.model_item: synchronous MAP + crystalloid input + urine output + creatinine/albumin in the same ICU stay
f_constrains.measured_quantity: chartevents, inputevents, outputevents, labevents joined on hadm_id/stay_id with chart times

f_constrains.model_item: arterial_pressure0_mmHg, venous_pressure0_mmHg, gfr0_ml_min, reabsorption_fraction0, bolus protocol
f_constrains.measured_quantity: same tables, larger n and full-population coverage

posts.not_downloaded_reason: credentialed access, DUA and CITI training required; PREREG.md 'Not redone' forbids fetching access-protected material in this lane
posts.why_it_matters: this is the single most important unexploited constraint for Q017: it is the only candidate that natively carries pressure, fluid volume and a renal marker on one stay-level time axis at hour resolution, i.e. exactly the 'synkrona perturbationsserier' the Q017 question demands. The eICU demo substitutes for it only partially (1039 unit stays carry MAP+intake+urine+creatinine, but the demo is 2520 stays, about 4 % of the full database).

posts.name: Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults (CARDIA), NHLBI BioLINCC
posts.license_verbatim: Data Use Agreement required; the study page offers 'Renew Existing Data Use Agreement' and 'Agreement Templates'
posts.access_policy_verbatim: Available data for request include exam data through Year 35 and outcomes and death data through 2022.
posts.d_format: SAS/Stata transport files and SAS export scripts, distributed per approved request

e_subjects.source: study page, verbatim: 'CARDIA is a population-based observational study of 5,115 participants aged 18-30 years recruited in 1985-1986'

f_constrains.model_item: arterial_pressure0_mmHg, gfr0_ml_min, ecf_volume0_ml, reabsorption_fraction0 - but longitudinally
f_constrains.measured_quantity: repeated clinic BP, weight, creatinine and albumin across up to 6 exam visits over 35 years in the same participant

posts.not_downloaded_reason: Data Use Agreement and a per-request approval by the study coordinating centre
posts.why_it_matters: the only identified candidate with a genuine repeated-measures design in a population cohort (as opposed to ICU stays): it is the natural test bed for whether a Q017-style parameter set transfers from one care episode to another, and for slow feedback time constants on a years scale. The cohort is 18-30 years old at entry, so it brackets the Davies-Shock 20-29 year group the model initialises from.

posts.name: OpenCap human movement data (Stanford, SimTK)
posts.excluded_reason: not_applicable: inputs/Q017_model.py is a lumped (0-D) haemodynamic model with no geometric, anatomical or inertial parameter, so a marker-based motion-capture dataset cannot constrain any of its parameters or outputs. Recorded here so the exclusion is on record rather than silent; the same reasoning applies to the Imperial College femur/tibia statistical shape models, VSD bone models and CT data mentioned in inputs/NIGHT_PREAMBLE.md section 7.
